fact_claims.verbatim: Ember 8 had a 3.9% failure rate at 55 °C
9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year
four incidents were not reported to a regulator

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, or injury/property-damage event involving a covered battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, followed by a complete incident report within 10 calendar days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk or requires customer action; otherwise, include it in the next scheduled safety communication.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units before market entry and after material design changes. A failure rate above 5% triggers prompt regulator notification, investigation, and a corrective-action and retest plan.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect must support secure remote emergency shut-off, with protections against unauthorized access and clear customer instructions. For units already installed when the requirement takes effect, manufacturers must provide remote shut-off through retrofit or an equivalent safe upgrade within 6 years, where technically feasible.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect must include built-in fire suppression designed and validated to reduce the risk of thermal propagation.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A notice requiring immediate action must be sent within 72 hours of determining that action is needed; other material safety information must be included in the next scheduled safety communication. Manufacturers must notify the relevant regulator and affected customers when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period.

document.section_notes: The final rules are mixed: S1 is weakened because only serious incidents are reportable and minor events lack deadlines. S2 is weakened because existing models are exempt from retesting and above-5% failures can continue under time-limited remediation, though the 55°C test and 5% trigger remain. S3 is weakened by a 24-month new-unit deadline and a 6-year retrofit, while S4 (36-month suppression) and S5 (mandatory recall at 8/100k, 72-hour urgent notices) are acceptable/safe. Overall the package favors Northwind, especially on testing, retrofit, and recall triggers.
